correctness.rationale: The all-minor scheme calculation is valid: after pivoting on a nonzero a_pq and dehomogenizing, invertible block elimination turns each Schur entry into a unit multiple of the corresponding pivot minor, and every three-minor vanishes modulo those entries. Eliminating off-pivot entries leaves disjoint relations s_i t_i=0 since 2 is invertible. This squarefree regular sequence proves reducedness, pure dimension n-2 and lci locally. A branch chooses one orientation of each remaining vertex relative to the pivot; the corresponding rank-one cross block is the indicated Segre, with distinct complete-bipartite support at its generic point. Zero rows are exactly pairs with both coordinates zero. At a geometric point each other pair contributes one smooth coordinate, so the displayed completed ring has z nodal factors. The displayed smooth-factor dimension is for geometric points, as in the residue-field base-change interpretation, not the local dimension at an arbitrary nonclosed scheme point before base change. Reduced row-w locus is the same section on n-1 vertices; its components have generically just one zero row, so no duplicates occur across choices of w. This works also at n=3, where fixed zero row leaves a projective point. Vandermonde gives each degree after summing Segre degrees, and normalization is the disjoint union of the normal components. Inspected verify.py, without executing it: the pivot determinant, support and finite GF(3) checks corroborate but do not prove the ideal equality or the general local statement. No affine-vertex or characteristic-two result is inferred.
